issue_comments.body: ### Reviewing PR #4949 - [ ] Read the branch diff against `origin/main` - [ ] Review Phase 12 babysit loop changes - [ ] Review Phase 12b follow-up sweep - [ ] Post review [View job run](https://github.com/skaile-ai/platform/actions/runs/35725564596) · `chore/ship-babysit`

**Claude finished @Frozen666's task in 2m 13s** —— [View job](https://github.com/skaile-ai/platform/actions/runs/35723570306)

---
### Re-review: PR #4949 — `ship` skill babysit changes

- [x] Read the new commit `b92063876` against `8dadaaada`
- [x] Re-check the 5 findings from the previous round
- [x] Verify the corrected `gh` commands against the live API
- [x] Post review

`b92063876` addresses **all five** findings from the previous round, and the corrections hold up against the live API — I re-ran each call on this PR rather than taking the commit's word for it. The three-source poll is the right shape: it is the only combination that carries a commit oid on every head-scoped signal, and the commit says so explicitly instead of leaving it as folklore.

### Previous-round findings

| # | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `reviewThreads` is not a `gh pr view --json` field; SHA filter had nothing to read; `headRefOid` fetched-but-unused | **Addressed.** `reviewThreads` is gone with a note on *why* the whole call exits non-zero. `headRefOid` is now the SHA authority over the local worktree HEAD, with the divergence rationale. The scope rules name the right accessors — verified: `reviews[]` → `{"commit":{"oid":"8dadaaad…"}}`, `pulls/4949/comments[]` → `{"commit_id":"8dadaaad…","original_commit_id":"8dadaaad…"}`. |
| 2 | Consumed-by-id inverts against a `track_progress` sticky comment | **Addressed, and the fix is verified live.** Keying on (id, `updated_at`) from the REST issue-comments endpoint works precisely because the edit-in-place shows up there — the previous round's comment reads `created_at 11:42:03` / `updated_at 11:46:02` under one id. The `- [ ]`-means-spinner rule is spelled out too. |
| 3 | Cutoff counted in a unit change (1) redefined | **Addressed.** `fix_rounds` is a separate counter incremented only on an actual push, the cutoff gates on it, `MAX_ROUNDS` is 6 → 10 as the runaway guard, and the reason the two must not be one counter is written down. Propagated through the summary table, MUST list, `triage_finding`, `classify_babysit_item`, the checklist and the anti-patterns table. |
| 4 | 12b re-entry unaccounted | **Addressed.** Shared counters/budget, 12b runs at most once, `EMIT babysit_done` moved past the re-entry, and Phase 13 now has an explicit "CI running" branch with the note that `mergeStateStatus,mergeable` catches BLOCKED but not PENDING. |
| 5 | Nit: empty rollup right after a push reads as `no-checks` | **Addressed.** ≥3 consecutive empty polls **and** ≥60s since the push, with the observation that a genuinely CI-less repo trips it a minute later at no cost. |

### New findings on this commit

**Important**

| # | Where | What |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [L753](https://github.com/skaile-ai/platform/pull/4949#discussion_r4071270627) | The loop can still spin on its own signal — the author just changed. (c) replies on threads *after* pushing, so those replies carry the new head's `commit_id` and are unconsumed at the new head SHA. The break fires, (b) finds nothing, a round burns. Worst on the decline path, which replies once per declined nit in exactly the rounds where the budget is tightest. One discard rule next to the SHA-scope list fixes it. |

**Nits**

- [L676](https://github.com/skaile-ai/platform/pull/4949#discussion_r4071270836) — the `- [ ]`-is-a-spinner test is stated over all top-level comments, so a human comment containing an unchecked task box is permanently ignored rather than deferred.
- [L742](https://github.com/skaile-ai/platform/pull/4949#discussion_r4071272050) — `declined (nit, fix_round <F>)` is off by one (`fix_rounds` increments after the push), contradicting L919's `from fix push <NIT_CUTOFF_ROUND>+1 on`.
- [L770](https://github.com/skaile-ai/platform/pull/4949#discussion_r4071272336) — Phase 12's "Babysit done…" print survives alongside 12b's new one; with the re-entry that's three prints for one babysit, the first two understating `<R>`.

### Checked and fine

- The cutoff arithmetic is consistent end to end: `fix_rounds < 3` at evaluation time means pushes 1–3 fix nits and push 4 declines, matching "the fourth fix push onward" and the `+1` in the final report header.
- Every downstream mention of the old round-based cutoff was updated — I grepped for stragglers and found none.
- Version 1.3.0 → 1.3.1 is right for a correctness fix to an unreleased-elsewhere skill; the #4944 drift note is untouched and still accurate.
- Still no changeset needed: `.claude/**` is outside `changeset-check.yml`'s paths and `ship` is not in `scripts/embed-builtin-skills.ts`.

Carrying forward, unchanged and still not a PR defect: this checkout's working tree holds a stale `version: 1.1.0` copy of the file while `HEAD` has 1.3.1. I reviewed `git show HEAD:…`, not the working tree — worth a glance locally in case it is more than a runner artifact.

*Nothing implemented — review only.*
 · branch [`chore/ship-babysit`](https://github.com/skaile-ai/platform/tree/chore/ship-babysit)
